requirement:
Saved configuration MUST remain distinct from resolved runtime configuration.
Serializing and deserializing a valid configuration MUST preserve its semantic
values, including explicit versus omitted settings. Optional fields MAY be
omitted on serialization; defaults and environment-derived values MUST NOT be
materialized into omitted fields. TOML comments and formatting need not
round-trip.

Loading configuration or running a configured feature MUST NOT rewrite the user
or project configuration as a side effect. Resolved credentials and live runtime
objects MUST NOT enter the serialized data structures. Explicitly supplied
credential values are permitted only in the fields documented by the authoring
feature; credentials resolved from a profile or environment MUST NOT be written
back to configuration.
rationale:
I found no gap in `requirements.configuration.serialization`. Every obligation has code that carries it out and a test that asserts the outcome.

- **Saved configuration is distinct from resolved runtime configuration.** The saved types in `src/config.rs` derive `Serialize` and `Deserialize`. `ResolvedAuthoringConfig` does not derive `Serialize`; it holds only the selected saved values and their source. `resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from` builds it by cloning the saved `BackendConfig`. Defaults are applied through accessors (`endpoint`, `api_key_from`, `effective_policy`, `effective_concurrency`, `options_json`) and never stored back into the saved structs.
- **Round trip preserves values, including explicit versus omitted settings.** Optional fields use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]`. `UserConfig::to_toml` and `WorkspaceConfig::to_toml` validate and serialize. Both `parse` functions decode and validate.
- **Defaults and environment-derived values are not materialized.**
  - `backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults`, `authoring_concurrency_defaults_overrides_and_invalid_values`, `authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips` and `openai_defaults_are_effective_only_and_explicit_values_win` assert that omitted settings stay absent from the serialized text and that explicit values round-trip.
  - `user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map` covers empty and populated maps and project selections.
  - `absent_and_minimal_configuration_are_distinct_and_read_only` and `workspace_discovery_uses_nearest_file_without_merging_or_rewriting_it` cover minimal and workspace round trips.
- **Loading or running a feature does not rewrite configuration.** The load, parse and resolve paths only read. The only non-test file writes in `src` are the evidence writes in `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_assessment]`. `absent_and_minimal_configuration_are_distinct_and_read_only` and `workspace_discovery_uses_nearest_file_without_merging_or_rewriting_it` check that the file contents are unchanged after loading. `authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file` and `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` run the CLI and check that the configuration files are byte-identical afterwards and that no user configuration is created.
- **Resolved credentials and live runtime objects stay out of the serialized structures.** Resolution happens only in `api_key_from` and in `RigProvider::connect` through `bedrock_sdk_loader`. `ollama_authentication_resolves_separately_and_rejects_missing_values` and `openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials` check that env-resolved keys are absent from `to_toml` output. `omitted_bedrock_profile_and_region_use_standard_sdk_resolution` checks that the Bedrock configuration is unchanged after SDK resolution and that the resolved key and secret are not in its serialized text.
- **Explicit credentials appear only in documented fields.** Credentials fit only the typed `BedrockCredentials`, `OllamaConfig.api_key` and `OpenAiConfig.api_key` fields (`SecretString`, with `deny_unknown_fields`). `explicit_credentials_round_trip_but_diagnostics_and_debug_redact_them` checks that explicit credentials round-trip and that invalid placements are rejected. Credentials resolved from a profile or the environment are never written back, as the tests above show.

Every test above carries a `{test}` reference to the requirement. I found no unspecified behavior in the `{impl}` code and no `{fixme}` references.
